fields.mechanism: Crack tip shielding effect that reduces fatigue crack growth rate by correlating crack growth with the loading force range ΔF in addition to the stress‑intensity range ΔK.
fields.intervention: Apply shot‑peening (or laser peening) to the rail head surface to introduce compressive residual stresses, thereby creating a crack‑tip shielding effect that impedes crack propagation under cyclic loads.
fields.expected_effect: Lower crack growth rates and extended fatigue life of the rail, resulting in improved resistance to fatigue fracture under service loading.
fields.falsification_test: Perform comparative high‑cycle fatigue tests on shot‑peened rail specimens versus untreated specimens, measuring crack growth rates and S‑N curves; a statistically significant reduction in growth rate in the treated samples would confirm the mechanism.
